newsitem.title: UK: OFT briefs Britain's Beckett on BA, American.
newsitem.headline: OFT briefs Britain's Beckett on BA, American.

text.p: Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) confirmed on Tuesday that it briefed the new Labour government's trade and industry minister Margaret Beckett on the proposed alliance between British Airways Plc and American Airlines.

But industry sources said the OFT has still not made any recommendations to Beckett, because it still has to agree terms which might satisfy both BA and American and critics of the controversial deal.
"There is to be a report and a conclusion. What she (Beckett) got is the report, but not the conclusion," said one source.
"We are still in negotiation with the airlines," said an OFT spokesman.
He said the interim report passed to Beckett on May 16 simply outlined the responses it had received from airlines and other interested parties to the proposals made last year for approving the deal.
The report was put on Beckett's desk four days before she met with European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert to discuss his objections to the deal.
But OFT officials declined to comment on an industry report that it was planning to meet with Van Miert's office on Wednesday to discuss the matter further.

The OFT and former trade minister Ian Lang proposed last December that BA and American should release 168 weekly take-off and landing slots at London Heathrow -- enough to operate 12 daily return flights -- to make room for competitors.
But rival airlines and the European Commission said more concessions were needed if BA and American were to be prevented from dominating the Anglo-U.S. transatlantic market with a 62 percent share.
BA said it expected to meet with the European Commission to discuss its concerns next week but a spokesman declined to give a precise date.

Agreement between Britain's new Labour government and Van Miert on how to handle the deal would head off a potential row between Britain and the European Commission over who has ultimate jurisdiction over the competition issues.
Van Miert had threatened to take Britain's previous Conservative government to the European Court of Justice if it went ahead and approved the deal on the basis of the Lang proposals.
